Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-side review of Seller Update draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller's package instructs us to treat clauses marked [STANDARD] as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to accept the disclosure framework and limitation package as agreed. That is not correct and has been disregarded. Nothing in our record shows Wattlebridge has agreed any of these positions; the [STANDARD] tags cover precisely the clauses most adverse to the Buyer. Every clause has been reviewed against the playbook. We should also tell Seller's counsel in the cover response that no clause is agreed until marked up and signed off by Amelia Frost.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** 20% is a conditional fallback available only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none exists.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three limbs; counter with playbook terms.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and convert a tipping basket into a deductible, materially shrinking recoverable loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a default that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the default wording silently extends the general regime to everything.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- Buyer wants: separate regime — 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright; insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.** Capping title at 20% means paying AUD 24m for shares with recourse limited to AUD 4.8m if title fails.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment carve-out across cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5.** This is a non-negotiable playbook item and no one on our side has authority to waive it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public registers (Sch 7; Disclosure Letter [1.1]-[1.2]); [1.4] denies any admission.
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only — no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject [1.1]-[1.2] and Sch 7 general disclosure; require matters to be fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope.** Whole-data-room disclosure would hollow out every warranty.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter of which Buyer or advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: deletion of the blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with SPA-N-006, would bar virtually all claims.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter [2] confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: effective consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion; not consent-on-delivery.
- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft as a Completion condition requiring unconditional effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m); reasonable endeavours is inadequate for a material customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter [3] confirms not repaid, no discharge.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release; require payout letter, repayment at Completion via funds flow, and executed discharges (DD-003 cl 9.2) as Completion deliverables.** Any post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval — neither is on the table.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure Letter [5] confirms not in funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded.
- Recommendation: **Reject; add a specific line item (bonus + superannuation + payroll tax + other on-costs) as Seller-funded Transaction Costs/Debt in the funds flow, with a Seller indemnity.** Completion-triggered bonuses will otherwise fall on the Company post-Completion, i.e. on the Buyer.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). Disclosure Letter [4]: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering ownership/title to SOW3 Project Materials, infringement and any claim by Ironquay, while preserving the cure (payment → transfer).
- Recommendation: **Reject as drafted; broaden the indemnity and add a pre-Completion covenant to pay and obtain a confirmatory assignment.** The AUD 180,000 is unverified either way, so the fix must work whether or not it is actually outstanding.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter [6]: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, written updates to Completion, and specific indemnity for notification/regulatory/third-party costs if it crystallises — without assuming a breach has occurred.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; add a pre-Completion covenant (preserve logs, investigate, update) and a specific indemnity for losses arising from the DD-006 incident.** We should neither concede nor assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or amount.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter [8] does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: an assessment of timing, scope and terminability before any pricing position; no automatic Debt treatment.
- Recommendation: **Hold; request DD-008/DD-011 contract terms, renewal dates and termination rights, and reserve position on Debt/working capital treatment.** Neither side's characterisation is supported yet, so do not concede "ordinary course" or demand a deduction.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: single general regime applied to all Claims (cl 12.3 default, 9.3/12.8/20.5, Tax/IP "settled under the general regime").
- Buyer wants: separate Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant categories with their own caps and periods, no hidden override.
- Recommendation: **Reject; restructure cl 12-13 into distinct categories and delete every "all Claims" catch-all.** The Seller's drafting collapses specific indemnities and covenants into the 20%/18-month regime by default.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by the share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter [10] concedes this is the source relied on and that Buyer has not verified.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence — ASIC company extract, PPSR search, share certificates, constitution/board minutes evidencing authority, and confirmation of no encumbrances beyond Riverlark.
- Recommendation: **Treat DD-012 as unverified; obtain independent searches and add Title warranties and Completion deliverables.** A supplied internal register is not proof of title, encumbrance status or authority.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- Buyer wants: terms remain OPEN pending separate Tax and IP regimes (own caps/periods); no unlimited liability position adopted.
- Recommendation: **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as OPEN and table separate regimes in our mark-up.** Nothing has been agreed, and folding them into the general regime is a back-door application of SPA-N-001/003/014.

---

**Summary for the deal team:** The Seller package is adverse on every limitation point and contains no agreed positions. The three items that go to deal value or deliverability — Bluefen (SPA-N-008), Riverlark (SPA-N-009) and bonuses (SPA-N-010) — should be flagged as Completion-critical in our cover letter. No fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release) is available without Amelia Frost's written sign-off, and none has been given.
